contract_tuple: C = (S, K, W, Q, P, M)

S.description: Feature, target, raw Replay, feature-construction, humidity-conditioning, and time-feature schema.

humidity_conditioning.order: Apply the causal EMA to raw H_in before constructing H_in_lag1 and H_in_lag2.
humidity_conditioning.replay_pre_block_state_semantics: Filtered H_in EMA state immediately preceding the first exported Replay seed row.
humidity_conditioning.field_initialization: Initialize the EMA state from the first valid Field H_in sample.

lag_policy.order: Construct lag-1 and lag-2 features after humidity conditioning.
lag_policy.lag1_baseline: T_in_lag1 and H_in_lag1 are the absolute-state baselines used by P for residual reconstruction.

time_feature_policy.replay_time_source: Exported epoch associated with the deterministic Replay row.
time_feature_policy.field_fallback: If civil time is unavailable, derive hour cyclic features from the millis-based synthetic hour; weekday=0 and month=1.

K.description: Frozen scaler definition, forward/inverse MinMax transforms, and input-bound policy.

input_bound_policy.python_reference: Clip each physical-domain input feature to its frozen X_MIN/X_MAX bounds before MinMax scaling.
input_bound_policy.firmware_runtime: Apply MinMax scaling using the same frozen X_MIN/X_MAX bounds, then clamp the normalized value to [0, 1].
input_bound_policy.equivalence: For the same X_MIN/X_MAX bounds, both forms are algebraically equivalent.

K.input_forward_scaling: Per-feature MinMax scaling to [0, 1] using X_MIN/X_MAX.
K.target_forward_scaling: Residual model targets delta_T_in and delta_H_in use MinMax scaling to [0, 1] using DY_MIN/DY_MAX.
K.target_inverse_scaling: Inverse MinMax using DY_MIN/DY_MAX recovers residuals in physical units before reconstruction in P.

W.description: Rolling-window, stride, Replay chronology, seed-row processing, and warm-up exclusion policy.
W.seed_row_policy: The two preceding raw rows advance the causal H_in EMA from the exported pre-block EMA state and initialize lag history. Seed rows are not counted as chronological evaluation rows and are excluded from reported metrics.
W.rolling_cardinality_rule: For W=24, stride=1, and n=24 reported valid events, 47 chronological rows are required: W + (n - 1).

execution_modes.field: Live-sensor chronology with the same post-acquisition rolling/window semantics.

Q.description: Tensor I/O shape, dtype, quantization metadata, representable-range saturation, and semantic output mapping.
Q.output_mapping: Output position/channel 0 maps to delta_T_in; output position/channel 1 maps to delta_H_in.

P.description: Post-processing order and residual absolute-state reconstruction contract.
P.mapping_source: Apply the semantic output mapping defined in Q before residual inverse scaling.
P.residual_inverse_scaling: Apply the DY_MIN/DY_MAX inverse transform defined in K to recover delta_T_in and delta_H_in in physical units.

M.description: Valid-event definition, conformance-update rule, Rolling-24 metric aggregation, rounding, and acceptance-policy reference.
M.valid_event_update_rule: Update conformance counts and Rolling-24 aggregation only for valid post-warm-up inference events.

conformance_checkpoints.p_star: Effective model tensor payload under Q.
conformance_checkpoints.o_raw: Raw model output bytes/metadata and decoded outputs under Q.
conformance_checkpoints.y_star: Mapped, inverse-scaled, reconstructed prediction under P.
conformance_checkpoints.predictions_and_metrics: Final predictions and Rolling-24 metric vector over valid events.

M.tolerance_policy_scope: Single shared stage-wise acceptance policy applied unchanged to all evaluated models and hardware targets; numeric thresholds are not duplicated here.

firmware_safety_guard.decoded_scaled_residual: If a decoded scaled residual is non-finite, firmware replaces it with 0.0 before DY inverse scaling.
firmware_safety_guard.reconstructed_prediction: If a reconstructed absolute prediction is non-finite, firmware falls back to the current acquired T_in or H_in value.
firmware_safety_guard.scope: These are firmware-only safety guards outside the shared Python↔firmware equivalence path; they are not clipping, calibration, or part of contract element P.
